The prepare script tests writability of the literal .git/config with test -w, and its successful status is required by && before husky runs; there is no negation (f1:113, s1–s3). The operator other accommodates this positive writability test.

The test -w predicate checks whether .git/config is writable, so an existing but unwritable file fails it (f1:113). The appropriate property is filesystem writability or permissions, rather than mere file or directory existence.

The provided file contains no fs.existsSync test of the package root's src directory; its postinstall entry only names a separate script whose contents are not supplied (f1:106). No supplied slice anchors c1 or the claimed build branch, so its portability purpose cannot be checked.

The husky region requires both successful command -v git and successful test -w .git/config, joined by && (f1:113, s2–s3). The expression c2 alone omits the independent Git availability condition; the trailing || true does not provide another path to husky.
The writability test conditionally enables invocation of husky through &&; failure skips that invocation (f1:113). It neither chooses a different payload nor changes an invocation target.

The script invokes husky when Git is available and .git/config is writable, giving the writable environment the activating side of the test (f1:113). The decision contains no analysis, CI, or sandbox detection.

The prepare script checks Git availability and writable Git configuration before invoking husky, and tolerates failure with || true (f1:113). This adapts preparation to whether the checkout supports the development tool, supporting portability.
